chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Do not eat from what has been killed by a predator, nor from that which has been beaten to death, strangled, fallen from a height, or gored, unless you find it alive and slaughter it properly.

key_terms.السَّبُعِ: a beast of prey or predator
key_terms.النَّطِيحَةِ: an animal gored by another animal
key_terms.الْمُتَرَدِّيَةِ: an animal that fell and died
key_terms.الْمُنْخَنِقَةِ: an animal that died by strangulation
key_terms.تُدْرِكَهُ: you reach or find it before death

ai.seo_question: Which animals are forbidden to eat unless they are found alive and properly slaughtered?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the impermissibility of eating certain animals that die through unlawful causes, such as predation, beating, strangulation, falling, or goring. It makes an exception if the animal is reached while still alive and then properly slaughtered according to the prescribed method.
